newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LABOUR LEADER SEEKS TO QUASH CONVICTION.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LABOUR LEADER SEEKS TO QUASH CONVICTION.

text.p: Jailed Indonesian labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan, who is seeking to overthrow his conviction on charges of inciting workers to strike, offered evidence on Monday that he had instead sought to prevent industrial action.

Lawyers for Pakpahan told the East Jakarta State Court that his union had called for a moratorium on strikes in April 1994, ahead of worker riots that month in the city of Medan in north Sumatra, rather than incite them to unrest.
Pakpahan has asked the court to process a request to the Supreme Court to review its decision in October 1996 to jail him for four years.

The 43-year-old labour activist, who is being treated for an infection in a lung and a clot in an artery, was convicted by a lower court in 1994 of inciting workers to demonstrate on April 14 and 15 that year, sparking anti-Chinese rioting in Medan in which one person died and there was widespread property damage.

The decision was quashed by the Supreme Court the next year, but in 1996, the court reversed its own decison. The move came after Pakpahan was arrested on subversion charges on July 30 last year in the wake of rioting in Jakarta.

Pakpahan's lawyers argued that new evidence from 11 witnesses showed the central board of his unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI) had sent a letter to its branches calling off strikes and protests from April 1994 until October that year.
"I read such a letter in early April 1994, but I don't remember the exact date. It forbade demonstrations and strikes," witness Soniman Lafau, deputy head of the SBSI's Medan branch, told the court.

Lafau and six other witnesses were asked on Monday to verify depositions they had given to Pakapahan's lawyers and underwent brief examinations by chief judge Tojib, prosecutor Fachmi and Pakpahan's chief counsel Bambang Widjojanto.
All seven witnesses, who were SBSI officials in April 1994, confirmed they had seen the letter.

Pakapahan's lawyers said they had 11 witnesses to call. However, Tojib asked the case be adjourned after two hours because of other commitments by the panel of three judges. The case will resume with the examination of the statements of the remaining four witnesses on Thursday.
Pakpahan's subversion trial was suspended in March after he was hospitalised suffering from vertigo. He was later diagnosed as suffering from a clot in his brain and an unidentified lung ailment.
